_comment: Human verdicts for candidates where the class rule in
scripts/scan-pub-item-usage.py gets the wrong answer. The scan can see
whether a name is referenced; it cannot see why an item exists. Anything
recorded here is reported with this verdict instead of the inferred one.
Keys are '<repo-relative file>::<item name>'. The scan fails if a key
names an item that no longer exists, so this file cannot rot into a list
of excuses for code that was already deleted.
'escalated' means the finding is real and too big to settle inside a
cleanup PR. Every escalated entry ends in a question addressed to whoever
owns the subsystem, because the answer changes behaviour rather than

crates/sbproxy-security/src/agent_verify.reason: StubResolver is exported from lib.rs as a test double for out-of-crate consumers to build against. Its builders are the API; narrowing them would leave a stub nobody can configure.
Same as with_ptr: part of the exported StubResolver builder surface.
Same as with_ptr. Narrowed to pub(crate) during this sweep and reverted: the lib-only build then warns, because the only in-crate caller is a test.
Same as with_ptr. It looked dead because the stub's forward-error branch had no test at all; that gap is now covered rather than the builder deleted.

crates/sbproxy-security/src/pii.rs::Rule.reason: Types the pub field CompiledRule::validator, so narrowing it is a private-in-public error rather than a cleanup.

crates/sbproxy-security/src/pii.rs::reda.reason: Called directly by the out-of-tree consumer. Also recorded in a doc comment at the definition.

crates/sbproxy-core/src/admin_compressio.reason: Types the argument of CompressionAuditSink::record, and that trait is pub, so narrowing this is a private-in-public error rather than a cleanup. Same shape as RuleValidator.
Types the error half of CompressionAuditSink::record on the same pub trait, so it fails the private-in-public bar for the same reason CompressionAuditEvent does.

crates/sbproxy-ai/src/guardrails/classif.reason: The only constructor that accepts an already-resolved Arc<dyn TextClassifier>, so it is the seam for injecting a custom classifier backend, and its own doc says so. Nothing in the request path injects one today, which is why the class rule reads it as over-exposed. `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate)` would compile, but it would delete the seam from release builds rather than narrow it.

crates/sbproxy-modules/src/policy/prompt.reason: The only constructor that takes an arbitrary Arc<dyn Detector> instead of going through the inventory registry, so it is the detector injection seam. Same shape as classifier::with_backend: narrowing it under cfg(test) compiles and removes the seam from release builds, which is a product decision rather than a visibility fix.

crates/sbproxy-observe/src/exemplars.rs:.reason: Its doc states the purpose: unit tests in other crates assert that a helper stamped an exemplar onto a metric without reaching into the private store. Only this crate's own test modules use it today, so cfg(test) pub(crate) would compile and would quietly remove the cross-crate seam the doc promises.

crates/sbproxy-ai/src/api_routes.rs::par.reason: The OpenAI-compatible endpoint parser has no production caller. sbproxy-core/src/server/ai_dispatch.rs:2320 classifies the request path with an inline `path == "/v1/chat/completions"` comparison instead, so two answers to 'which endpoint is this' exist and only one runs. Question for the AI gateway owner: is the inline comparison the intended classifier, in which case parse_endpoint and the AiEndpoint enum go, or should dispatch route through this parser so every endpoint shape is recognised in one place? Thirteen tests and a public enum ride on the answer.

crates/sbproxy-core/src/compression_runt.reason: Resolves the route's default compression runtime and panics if the compiled default is missing, so it reads as the invariant check for a compiled set. Every caller is a test, including the one in server/ai_dispatch.rs. Question for the compression owner: does the dispatch path resolve the default some other way, in which case two definitions of 'the default' can disagree silently, or should it call this?

crates/sbproxy-core/src/key_plane.rs::in.reason: The production install path stores straight into the slot at key_plane.rs:940 and bypasses this wrapper; every caller of the wrapper is a test. Two ways to install the live key plane is the kind of split where one of them skips a future invariant. Question for the key-plane owner: should the production path call install_key_plane, or should the wrapper go and the tests store directly?

crates/sbproxy-mesh/src/metrics.rs::EVIC.reason: Answered on WOR-2225: graceful leave is unimplemented, not mishandled. There is no leave message anywhere on the wire (GossipMsg carries Heartbeat, Join, Ping, Ack, PingReq, IndirectAck; MeshMessage carries MembershipUpdate, Ping, Pong) and no shutdown path sends one, so a node that exits cleanly is evicted by the failure detector under probe_timeout or dead_timeout like any corpse. Building it is a wire change plus a lifecycle hook, not a bug fix. The constant is kept so the label value stays reserved, and the doc comments that used to promise a LeaveRequest handler now say it does not exist.

crates/sbproxy-transport/src/grpc/frame..reason: Answered on WOR-2225: the strict decoder is correct where it is called, and this one is not dead code so much as code for a direction that is not wired yet. grpc/web.rs:80 is the request path, and gRPC-Web only folds trailers into the body because a browser cannot read them off a response; a request has no trailers to fold, since gRPC carries none in that direction at all. So decode_all rejecting 0x80 there is the spec-correct behaviour, and it errors rather than misparsing. This walker is the response-direction counterpart, which the proxy does not need while it is the gRPC-Web server rather than a client of one. Tests now pin the split in both directions so the question does not get reopened.
